items.title: Celebrating 20 Years of Open Movies
items.summary_original: This year we are celebrating 20 years of making Open Movies. 17 titles, all different and beautiful in their own way. We want to thank you for being a part of this journey – without the community support, all of these projects would not be possible! To celebrate the 20 years of Open Movies in a special way during the Blender Conference 2026, we have created an installation that represents the projects frame by frame. And in the spirit of sharing and being open, visitors of the exhibition can take a frame with them. 20 years of Open Movies exhibition at Blender Conference 2026 Thank you for doing your part. Let’s see what the next decade of open filmmaking will bring!
items.title_de: Wir feiern 20 Jahre Open Movies

Um das 20-jährige Bestehen von Open Movies während der Blender-Konferenz 2026 auf besondere Weise zu feiern, haben wir eine Installation geschaffen, die die Projekte Bild für Bild darstellt. Und im Sinne des Teilens und der Offenheit können Besucher der Ausstellung einen Rahmen mitnehmen. 20 Jahre Open Movies-Ausstellung auf der Blender Conference 2026 Vielen Dank für Ihren Beitrag. Mal sehen, was das nächste Jahrzehnt des offenen Filmemachens bringen wird!

items.title: Show your support for Blender projects
items.summary_original: A donation to the Blender Development Fund has always been a non-targeted form of support that the Blender project further distributes as it sees fit. This will stay the same: the established process brings balance to development activities, ensuring that high-demand features go hand in hand with the necessary but sometimes invisible maintenance and quality-of-life improvements. However, from an individual donor point of view, the act of supporting a specific activity carries more weight and comes with a sense of purpose. It is also important for the Blender project to know which features have the most impact for supporters of the Blender Development Fund. items.title_de: Zeigen Sie Ihre Unterstützung für Blender-Projekte
items.summary_de: Eine Spende an den Blender Development Fund ist seit jeher eine nicht zielgerichtete Form der Unterstützung, die das Blender-Projekt nach eigenem Ermessen weiterverteilt. Das wird auch so bleiben: Der etablierte Prozess sorgt für Ausgewogenheit bei den Entwicklungsaktivitäten und stellt sicher, dass stark nachgefragte Funktionen mit den notwendigen, aber manchmal unsichtbaren Wartungs- und Lebensqualitätsverbesserungen einhergehen. Aus der Sicht eines einzelnen Spenders hat die Unterstützung einer bestimmten Aktivität jedoch mehr Gewicht und ist mit einem Sinn verbunden. Für das Blender-Projekt ist es auch wichtig zu wissen, welche Funktionen für Unterstützer des Blender Development Fund den größten Einfluss haben. Um dieses Problem zu beheben, haben wir kürzlich die Funktion „Zeigen Sie Ihre Unterstützung“ zur Spendenseite und zur Blender-Roadmap hinzugefügt. Nun, eine Dona

items.title: LOEWE’s paris runway occupies an ethereal arena by casper mueller kneer
items.summary_original: architecture for looking For Loewe ’s Spring Summer 2027 show, the runway rises off the usual single plane. Inside a temporary white volume in the courtyard of Paris’ Château de Vincennes, Casper Mueller Kneer Architects has built a circular, two-story arena where guests look across, down, and through the space at one another. Models move along a runway that snakes between angular benches at ground level, while another band of viewers occupies the balcony above. Fashion becomes something seen from several heights at once. The architecture borrows its basic geometry from places where an audience traditionally surrounds an event. items.title: color-shifting light sculpture suspends above orchestra at walt disney concert hall
items.summary_original: RADIANCE Translates Fire Into Light at Walt Disney Concert Hall RADIANCE is a light sculpture installation by Grimanesa Amorós, commissioned by the Los Angeles Philharmonic and presented at Walt Disney Concert Hall across three consecutive performances. Conceived to accompany Alexander Scriabin’s Prometheus: The Poem of Fire, Op. 60 (1910), the work takes fire as its subject, resolving into the form of a pulsing spark suspended above the orchestra. The installation draws on two cultural references: Prometheus, who gave fire to humanity, and Viracocha, the Incan creator deity. Together, they frame light as a carrier of knowledge and a medium of transformation. items.title: Building A UX ROI Case That Survives The Boardroom
items.summary_original: Sooner or later, a CFO looks at your wireframes and asks what any of it actually does for the bottom line. Storyboards don’t answer that question, and the era when a 5-minute pitch could answer it ended, unfortunately, a while ago. These days, if you want to win budget, buy-in, and backing for UX , the design has to be provably good for the business, not only for the people using it. And proving that takes more than taping a dollar sign to a redesign. You have to understand how your organization defines value in the first place, how it measures that value, and how a credible line gets drawn between a design initiative and an outcome leadership already cares about. items.title: Are we cooked?!
items.summary_original: Are we cooked?! It's the question every designer is quietly asking right now. So we asked it to 30 leading design voices. "Are we cooked?!" is a 240-page hardcover book collecting 30 interviews with designers, artists, and creatives across the industry, all wrestling with what AI actually means for their craft. The voices range from design leads at LVMH , Kurppa Hosk , Mutabor , KMS TEAM or Stan Hema to independent artists like Boris Eldagsen . The answers couldn't be more contradictory. AI is "a partner". AI is "fast-food culture". AI is "basically an average-calculator". We're "100% cooked". We're "not cooked at all". The book doesn't resolve these contradictions. It documents them, as a snapshot of a discourse moving faster than anyone can keep up with. And that's exactly why it's print

items.title: Stop Treating CSS Container Queries Like Traditional Media Queries
items.summary_original: To be completely honest with you, I missed the news when CSS Container Queries first shipped. And when I finally heard about it, my very first thought was, “Why exactly do I need this when media queries already exist?” I’m not proud of that reaction, knowing what I know now, but it was comforting to know that I wasn’t alone. In fact, there are legions of us out there. What baffles me is that container queries aren’t a new feature, as it currently sits at around 94% browser support . And yet, very few people are actually using it. According to the State of CSS survey, 86% of developers are aware of container queries, but only 41.4% actually use them. Surveys can be biased and not completely representative of our entire field, but this one is certainly the best indicator we’ve got. Kevin Pow

items.title: Ellie Campbell turns club nights into hand-painted, gloriously wonky animations
items.summary_original: Growing up in Weston-super-Mare, the artist found an escape in cartoons and animation. Now, she's turning that lifelong obsession into painstakingly painted rotoscoped works that are full of life and cracking dance moves. There is something wonderfully stubborn about painting an animation frame by frame. While the moving image is usually associated with speed and technology, Ellie Campbell is interested in exactly what happens when you slow the whole thing down and use a paintbrush to create the visuals. Her hand-painted rotoscope animations take real footage and pull it apart, exaggerating bodies and gestures into familiar scenes – throwing shapes on the dancefloor, watching a duck swim across the pond or sipping a cold frosty pint to name just a few. items.title: FONS HICKMANN
items.summary_original: The Brandenburgisches Landesmuseum für moderne Kunst (Brandenburg Museum of Modern Art) presents a substantial solo exhibition of posters by Fons Hickmann at the Dieselkraftwerk Cottbus, bringing together work from more than three decades. The exhibition spans early and recent posters, international commissions, cultural projects, political interventions and self-initiated work. Rather than presenting a strictly chronological retrospective, it traces the continuities, shifts and contradictions within a practice in which commissioned design and autonomous artistic work have increasingly come together. Typography, image and language form the basis of Hickmann’s work, often engaging with cultural, political and social subjects. Many of the posters shown have received international recognition

You click menus, adjust range sliders, fill out multi-step forms, deal with cookie pop-ups, and open dozens of browser tabs just to cross-reference basic information. Angetrieben durch Fortschritte in der künstlichen Intelligenz und großen Sprachmodellen ist eine neue Generation von Web-Tools auf dem Vormarsch

A nightclub does not have a conventional audience. There is no fixed row of seats, no clear division between stage and auditorium, and no guarantee that the person who enters will remain a spectator. Once inside, bodies, sound, light, fashion and architecture begin to become one. The room changes as people move, and the people inside are part of what everyone else is experiencing. items.title: LinkedIn für Kreative: sichtbar werden, Vertrauen aufbauen, Kund:innen gewinnen
items.summary_original: Wie können Kreative LinkedIn strategisch nutzen, um sichtbar zu werden, Vertrauen aufzubauen und relevante Auftraggeber:innen zu erreichen? Karolina Zolubak zeigt in zwei Stunden, wie Profil, Netzwerk und Content zusammenspielen – und wie daraus eine LinkedIn-Strategie für den eigenen Arbeitsalltag entsteht. Viele Kreative sind auf LinkedIn zwar angemeldet, nutzen die Plattform aber nicht strategisch. Das Profil gleicht einem digitalen Lebenslauf, das Netzwerk ist eher zufällig gewachsen und beim Thema Content fehlt oft ein Plan. Dabei bietet LinkedIn gerade für Kreative die Möglichkeit, die eigene Expertise sichtbar zu machen, Beziehungen zu potenziellen Kund*innen aufzubauen und dafür zu sorgen, dass relevante Menschen auf die eigene Arbeit aufmerksam werden. Im Einführungsseminar zeigt

items.title: Visual Intelligence: Wie Informationsdesign die Welt retten kann
items.summary_original: In der aktuellen PAGE 03.2026 gehen wir der Frage nach, wie Design die Welt retten kann. Interessante Antworten bietet dazu auch die Schau »On Display. Wie Grafikdesign uns gestaltet«. Mit dabei: das Studio visual intelligence. Mit dessen Mitgründer Robin Coenen haben wir über die Kraft von Informationsdesign gesprochen – und über Data Driven Empowerment. visual intelligence: Informationsdesign Dekoloniale Im Museum Angewandte Kunst in Frankfurt am Main wird in der Ausstellung » On Display « gerade gezeigt, » Wie Grafikdesign uns gestaltet «. Die Schau erinnert daran, dass alles um uns herum gestaltet ist und prägt, wie wir handeln, fühlen, die Welt wahrnehmen – von der Müsliverpackung über die Schilder der Bushaltestellen zu unseren Apps. Drei Positionen hat Kurator Dr. Jonas Deuter ausge
